findings.title: Uncapped liquidated damages at excessive daily rate
findings.deviation: The clause imposes a 2% daily penalty on total fees with no cap, whereas the standard allows 0.5% per week of the affected milestone capped at 5%.
findings.impact: AtliQ would face extreme financial exposure for minor delays if this clause were applied against them, and it is commercially punitive for the vendor.
findings.quote: Vendor shall pay AtliQ, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Fees for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; LDs as the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.
findings.linkedQuote: Client may claim a contractual penalty (Vertragsstrafe) of 0.5% of the Milestone Fee of the affected Milestone for each full week of delay, up to a maximum of 5% of that Milestone Fee.

findings.title: Pay-when-paid structure with 120-day limit
findings.deviation: Payment is contingent on AtliQ receiving funds from the client and allows up to 120 days, violating the 45-day maximum and the ban on pay-when-paid terms.
findings.impact: This pushes all cash flow risk onto the subcontractor and creates a payment window far exceeding AtliQ's acceptable standard.
findings.quote: AtliQ's obligation to pay any invoice is conditional upon AtliQ's receipt of payment from the End Client for the corresponding services. AtliQ shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within fifteen (15) days after AtliQ receives the corresponding payment from the End Client, and in any event not later than one hundred and twenty (120) days after AtliQ's receipt of the invoice.
findings.counterPosition: Payment within 30 days of receipt of invoice (45 days maximum); delete pay-when-paid conditions.

findings.title: One-sided unlimited liability for vendor
findings.deviation: The agreement caps AtliQ's liability but explicitly states that the vendor's liability is unlimited, including for indemnities.
findings.impact: AtliQ would never accept uncapped liability as a supplier; this lack of mutuality creates an unfair and high-risk engagement for the vendor.
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE VENDOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING VENDOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS.
findings.counterPosition: Mutual cap of 1x fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.

findings.title: Failure to assign IP rights to AtliQ
findings.deviation: Vendor retains ownership of all outputs and only grants a non-transferable license, whereas the client contract requires AtliQ to transfer exclusive rights.
findings.impact: AtliQ will be unable to deliver the promised exclusive rights to Rheinwerk Analytics, resulting in a direct breach of the main services agreement.
findings.quote: Vendor shall retain all right, title and interest in and to its tools, labelling platform, scripts, ontologies, annotation guidelines developed by Vendor, and annotation outputs, including all intellectual property rights therein (collectively, "Vendor IP").
findings.counterPosition: Contractor must assign all right, title, and interest in the Deliverables (excluding pre-existing tools) to AtliQ.
findings.linkedQuote: Except for PipeKit, Client shall acquire the exclusive, perpetual, transferable and unrestricted right of use in all Work Results created specifically for Client, upon full payment of the relevant Milestone Fee.

findings.title: Vendor indemnifies AtliQ's own negligence
findings.deviation: The indemnity requires the vendor to cover losses even if caused by AtliQ's own negligence.
findings.impact: AtliQ's standard prohibits indemnifying the other party for its own negligence; this represents an unreasonable risk transfer to the subcontractor.
findings.quote: in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any AtliQ Indemnitee.
findings.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence.

findings.title: No payment for work in progress
findings.deviation: AtliQ is only required to pay for accepted deliverables upon convenience termination, excluding work in progress.
findings.impact: The vendor would not be compensated for efforts spent on ongoing milestones, which violates AtliQ's standard for fair termination compensation.
findings.quote: AtliQ's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by AtliQ prior to the effective date of termination; AtliQ shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
findings.counterPosition: AtliQ must pay for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress.
findings.linkedQuote: Upon termination by Client for convenience (§ 648 BGB), Supplier shall be entitled to the agreed remuneration for services rendered plus compensation for committed costs.

findings.title: One-way confidentiality obligations
findings.deviation: The confidentiality Article only binds the vendor to protect AtliQ's information and does not protect the vendor's information.
findings.impact: AtliQ would reject a one-way NDA as a supplier; the playbook requires confidentiality terms to be mutual in substance.
findings.quote: Vendor shall (a) hold Confidential Information in strict confidence, (b) use it only to perform the Services, and (c) disclose it only to those Vendor Personnel with a need to know...
findings.counterPosition: Make the confidentiality definitions and obligations mutual.
findings.linkedQuote: The Parties shall keep confidential all business and trade secrets of the other Party that come to their knowledge...

findings.title: Missing Data Processing Agreement flow-down
findings.deviation: The agreement contains no data processing terms or DPA despite the vendor handling personal data like technician names.
findings.impact: AtliQ will be in breach of GDPR and the Rheinwerk contract's requirement to flow down data protection obligations to sub-processors.
findings.quote: Source data comprises ... technician names, shift identifiers and free-text notes
findings.counterPosition: Execute a Sub-DPA with the vendor back-to-back with the Client's Annex 3.
findings.linkedQuote: To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Client, the Parties shall conclude the Data Processing Agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR attached as Annex 3

findings.title: Missing evidence of client consent
findings.deviation: The agreement does not confirm that Rheinwerk Analytics has provided the required written consent for this specific subcontractor.
findings.impact: If AtliQ engages the vendor without prior client consent, it will be in immediate breach of § 15.3 of the client contract.
findings.quote: Vendor shall perform the Services described in the Engagement Schedule.
findings.counterPosition: Obtain prior written consent from Rheinwerk Analytics before finalizing the subcontract.
findings.linkedQuote: Supplier may subcontract parts of the services only with Client's prior written consent.

fine.note: Governing law is set to Indian law, which is correct for AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd.
No non-compete or restrictive covenants are imposed on AtliQ.
15-day acceptance period is within normal commercial standards.
